--- the fix commands the report prints are real commands ---
Each finding carries a `fix` field. Running both of them and re-scanning
must return the fixture to clean, exit 0. That is what makes the report
actionable rather than merely descriptive.

--- exclusions ---
An exclusion prefix must skip a whole directory, must NOT match a partial
directory name, and must still list what it skipped.

=== $ cd capture_work/repo && mkdir -p generated && printf '#!/usr/bin/env python3\n' > generated/gen.py && git add -- generated/gen.py && python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . --quiet -o r.json; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('r.json'));print('findings',[f['path'] for f in d['findings']])" ===
findings ['generated/gen.py']
exit=0

=== $ cd capture_work/repo && python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . --exclude generated --quiet -o r2.json; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('r2.json'));print('findings',[f['path'] for f in d['findings']]);print('skipped',[(s['path'],s['reason'],s.get('prefix')) for s in d['skipped']])" ===
findings []
skipped [('blob.bin', 'binary', None), ('generated/gen.py', 'excluded', 'generated')]
exit=0

=== $ cd capture_work/repo && python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . --exclude gen --quiet -o r3.json; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('r3.json'));print('does prefix gen exclude generated/ ?',[s['path'] for s in d['skipped'] if s['reason']=='excluded'])" ===
does prefix gen exclude generated/ ? []
exit=0

--- CLI contract ---
Setup errors are exit 2 and say why on stderr. They must never be
confused with exit 1, which means "mismatches found".

=== $ python3 shebangmode.py --root /no/such/dir/zzz ===
shebangmode.py: error: --root '/no/such/dir/zzz' is not a directory
exit=2

=== $ python3 shebangmode.py --root / ===
shebangmode.py: error: not inside a Git checkout: '/' (fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git)
exit=2

=== $ mkdir -p capture_work/repo/sub && python3 shebangmode.py --root capture_work/repo/sub ===
shebangmode.py: error: --root 'capture_work/repo/sub' is inside a Git checkout but is not its root; the root is '..' relative to it. Scanning a subdirectory would silently check only part of the index and could report 'ok' for a repository that does not satisfy the rule.
exit=2

The last record is the one that found a real defect in this tool. git -C
DIR ls-files walks UP to the enclosing repository, so a directory nested
inside a checkout does not make git fail -- it returns the tracked files
at or below DIR, which for a fresh subdirectory is none. The first
version of shebangmode.py printed "status":"ok" and exited 0 for exactly
that input: a silent pass on a repository it had not looked at. --root
must now be the top of a checkout. The unit tests missed it because they
used a directory OUTSIDE any repository, where git really does fail.

The subdirectory used above is inside the FIXTURE repository this script
built, not inside the surrounding checkout. An earlier version put the
scratch directory in the surrounding tree, which made this record say
"is not its root" here and "not inside a Git checkout" when
regen-preflight re-ran it in its .git-stripped copy -- a transcript that
could not reproduce. `--root /` covers the no-repository-at-all case with
a path that means the same thing on every machine.

=== $ cd capture_work/repo && python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . -o /no/such/dir/zzz/out.json ===
shebangmode.py: error: cannot write --output: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/no/such/dir/zzz/out.json'
exit=2

--- determinism: two runs, byte-identical JSON ---

=== $ cd capture_work/repo && python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . --quiet -o d1.json; python3 ../../shebangmode.py --root . --quiet -o d2.json; cmp d1.json d2.json && echo BYTE_IDENTICAL_two_runs ===
BYTE_IDENTICAL_two_runs
exit=0
